knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: API return type contract violation under tensor subclass dispatch
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: APIs that construct structured return objects may bypass their documented return-type wrapper when dispatch goes through a Tensor subclass, causing the returned object to violate the API contract.

risk_dimensions.shape: Reduction paths with dim arguments, including edge/negative dim values and zero-sized or singleton dimensions
risk_dimensions.dtype: Different tensor dtypes may influence dispatch and subclass behavior
risk_dimensions.memory: Subclass wrappers can alter storage layout or metadata assumptions
risk_dimensions.device: Different devices may expose distinct wrapper dispatch or structured return paths
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Presence of Tensor subclass instances changes dispatch and may bypass standard API return-type construction

failure_mechanism.description: The implementation constructs structured return values at the API boundary. When a Tensor subclass is involved, dispatch may take a path that returns a plain tuple or container instead of the documented structured object, exposing a contract mismatch.

input_exploration: Wrap base tensors with multiple Tensor subclass types, including lightweight and as_subclass wrappers
Vary shapes, dtypes, devices, and subclass identity while preserving the reduction-with-dim call path
Use dim arguments with positive, negative, and edge dimension values
Exercise both dim-provided and no-dim return paths to compare return-type behavior
constraint_awareness: Documented return types may differ for reduction-with-dim versus full-reduction calls
Tensor subclass dispatch can bypass API-level return-type wrappers
Return-type contracts should be checked under wrapper or proxy inputs, not only plain tensors
oracle_strategy: Check the returned object type against the documented structured return type
Verify expected named attributes or fields exist and are accessible on the result
Treat plain tuples, missing fields, or type mismatches as incorrect output

transferability.reason: The principle applies to any API that constructs structured return objects and may dispatch differently when tensor subclasses or proxy objects are used. Testing the documented return-type contract under subclass or wrapper inputs is broadly applicable beyond the original API.

llm_reasoning_guidance.important_considerations: Focus on API return-type contracts when Tensor subclasses or dispatch wrappers are involved. Vary subclass types and dim arguments to expose paths that may bypass structured return construction.
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that wrap base tensors in subclasses, call reduction-style APIs with dim arguments, and assert the return object matches the documented structured type rather than a plain container. Avoid hard-coding the original API's named type; use type and attribute checks derived from the API documentation.
